text:
Zine Park: hello! Zine here 5 joining Design today. i'm hybrid (oakland/SF) and my hobbies include fermenting kombucha, rescuing office succulents, and terrible puns. any tips for where to hide a SCOBY starter in the office fridge without causing a biohazard incident? :herb:
WelcomeBot: welcome to Redwood, Zine! :wave: Check the #new-hires guide for fridge etiquette. You'll also get a welcome lunch invite.
Eli T: welcome Zine! we have a small shelf in the lounge fridge reserved for experiments. label it clearly and maybe wrap the jar? also FYI the facilities team likes to be looped in for anything long-term.
Noor: hi Zine 5 i'm facilities 5 happy to approve a temporary spot. if you're bringing a SCOBY pls put a note on it with a contact and date. also would love to trade plant cuttings if you rescue succulents. :seedling:
Zine Park: noted on the label 5 i will standardize on "Zine's Bubble Lab" + phone. ha. thanks Noor! happy to swap cuttings 5 i have a variegated sedum.
Cassidy R: welcome!! also re: kombucha, we run a weekly rooftop hang on thursdays where people bring snacks and drinks 5 perfect low-stakes spot to introduce the brew.
Maya C: hey Zine 5 if you ever need an extra jar or filter cloth i have spares. and we have a "kitchen experiments" note board so people know what smells to expect. :laughing:
Eli T: pro tip: keep the jar sealed-ish and put it on the bottom shelf. label with date made and whether it's flavored. people worry less about mystery jars this way.
Zine Park: love these tips. i'll bring a small jar to the rooftop on Thursday and promise not to start a SCOBY cult. also game for a plant swap 5 i'll DM pics. thanks for the warm welcome everyone! :sparkles:
Noor: added you to the SF office thread so you get invites. welcome aboard! :tada:
Zine Park: cheers! i'll bring extra kombucha for sampling at the rooftop. first round's on me. :beers:
